newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan Orimulsion sales rise 17 pct - Bitor.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan Orimulsion sales rise 17 pct - Bitor.

text.p: Exports of Venezuela's trademark boiler fuel Orimulsion climbed 17 percent to 4.2 million tonnes in 1996, state oil subsidiary Bitumenes Orinoco (Bitor) said in a statement on Wednesday.

Cost cutting through new technology helped the company make 25 billion Bolivars ($53 million) operating profit before depreciation and amortisation in 1996, while net profit for the year exceeded 2.6 billion Bolivars ($5.5 million). Bitor gave no comparative figures.
The rise in exports was largely due increasing use of the bitumen-based fuel in China, Lithuania, Japan, Denmark and Canada.
Bitor, a subsidiary of state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela, said new technology, especially horizontal well drilling, had cut the cost of production significantly.

The use of Orimulsion in power stations has been opposed by environmental groups in the United States and Europe on the grounds that it is a "dirty fuel". In sea trials, Bitor said it was able to achieve an 82 percent clean-up rating in the open sea and 94 percent in a loading terminal.
